channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: Apple adds $49.99 intelligence usage packs for Logic Pro AI features
item.description: Apple introduced one‑time $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs that let Logic Pro users extend access to cloud‑based AI assistants. The packs roll over month‑to‑month, expire after 12 months, and are expected to roll out to other Creator Studio apps later this month. It shows Apple moving from free AI access to a paid model, affecting how creators budget for AI‑enhanced workflows.

item.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 models
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. The models are designed for open-ended technical work and generate outputs up to 30% faster than the 5.1 versions. The release introduces updated models with improved coding, reasoning, and vision capabilities, priced lower than previous versions while offering an optional fast mode.

item.title: ChatGPT Enterprise now available in AWS Marketplace
item.description: OpenAI made ChatGPT Enterprise available through AWS Marketplace. The integration helps organizations simplify procurement using existing AWS purchasing and billing relationships. This availability simplifies procurement for organizations by allowing them to use their existing AWS billing and purchasing relationships to buy ChatGPT Enterprise.

item.title: Former US DOE staffers launch modular data center firm Mavria with $130M
item.description: Former U.S. Department of Energy staffers launched modular data center firm Mavria, raising $130 million across pre-seed and seed rounds at a $1 billion valuation. The funding was led by Paradigm, with participation from AMP PBC, Liquid 2, Critical Frontier, and Dream Ventures. The launch highlights how investors are channeling large amounts of capital into alternative infrastructure solutions intended to bypass traditional construction and power grid constraints for AI workloads.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Ember lightweight reasoning model
item.description: Meta Superintelligence Lab released Muse Ember, its lightest and most cost-efficient AI model yet, priced at $0.10 per million input tokens. The model is designed for repetitive agent execution tasks such as tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, and long document parsing. The release introduces a lower-cost reasoning model intended for high-volume agent workflows, offering an alternative to small models from competitors like Anthropic and OpenAI.

item.title: Nvidia intervention leads to Commerce chip smuggling probe being moved to DOJ
item.description: U.S. Commerce Department investigators probing Singapore‑based Megaspeed for diverting Nvidia AI chips to China were transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia contacted the agency. The probe began in late 2024 following discovery of Nvidia GPUs in a Malaysian data centre. The shift to the Justice Department raises the prospect of criminal charges and highlights how export‑control enforcement can be affected by corporate actions.

item.title: Trump says DOJ threatened top AI executive with jail over misconduct
item.description: In a 60 Minutes interview, Donald Trump claimed the Department of Justice threatened a top executive at a major artificial intelligence company with arrest over alleged misconduct. Trump did not name the individual or company involved in the incident. This highlights the use of direct federal legal threats by the administration to address alleged misconduct among leaders of major artificial intelligence companies.

item.title: Disney and Adobe partner to build proprietary generative AI models
item.description: Disney and Adobe signed a multiyear deal to build proprietary, artist-led generative AI models using Adobe Firefly Foundry for Disney's production pipeline. The partnership gives Disney early access to AI technology for its theme parks, cruise line, and ESPN graphics. This multiyear partnership demonstrates how major entertainment companies are integrating proprietary, custom-built generative AI models directly into large-scale production pipelines across media, theme parks, and sports broadcasting.

item.title: EU's proposed Digital Fairness Act targets addictive features and AI relationships
item.description: The European Commission is scheduled to consider the Digital Fairness Act, a proposal that would require companies to let adults disable addictive features and target AI systems that simulate relationships. The draft law also addresses manipulative app design, hard-to-cancel subscriptions, and consumer harm estimated at €7.9 billion annually. The Digital Fairness Act would expand EU consumer protection law to cover digital practices and traders not reached by the Digital Services Act.

item.title: Former DOJ antitrust officials launch AI legal startup FluxCap
item.description: Former Justice Department antitrust officials Jonathan Kanter and Doha Mekki have launched an AI-native legal tech startup called FluxCap to help plaintiffs build cases against large corporations. The startup raised $6 million in seed funding and its platform is already in use in active litigation matters seeking over $1 billion in damages. The venture brings prominent former government antitrust enforcers into the private legal tech sector, building AI tools specifically intended to assist plaintiffs in taking on deep-pocketed tech giants and other monopolies.

item.title: Spines raises $64 million to automate book publishing with AI agents
item.description: Spines announced a $64 million financing package – $29 million Series A‑1 equity led by Zeev Ventures and a $35 million non‑dilutive growth loan from Twelve. The Israeli AI‑publishing platform now reports a $50 million annual revenue run rate. The funding shows investor confidence in AI tools that can streamline the entire publishing workflow for authors.

item.title: Nvidia introduces robot simulation tools and GR00T 2 at CoRL
item.description: NVIDIA introduced open robotics technologies at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, Texas, including the GR00T 2 world action model and simulation tools. Two NVIDIA papers were named finalists for the Best Paper Awards out of thousands of submissions. These advancements help researchers train robots on complex manipulation tasks and evaluate performance across changing conditions.

item.title: Automattic launches Spacefast to host and deploy AI-generated apps
item.description: WordPress owner Automattic has launched Spacefast, a new service that provides backend infrastructure like databases and authentication for AI-generated websites and applications. The platform connects with various AI agents and allows users to deploy projects via Git repositories or directly from supported chatbots. As AI tools enable non-technical users to generate application prototypes quickly, infrastructure providers are building dedicated rails to bridge the gap between AI code generation and live web deployment.

item.title: Google expands TPU family with TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max systems
item.description: Google announced two eighth-generation Tensor Processing Unit systems: the TPU 8tx for secure confidential inference paired with AMD CPUs, and the TPU 8i Max dual-chip package for long-context window tasks, scheduled to launch in 2027. The hardware additions are paired with new developer software including native PyTorch support and an open-source XLA Serving Engine. Google's expansion of its custom silicon lineup with systems tailored for confidential workloads and memory-intensive agents gives enterprises and developers new infrastructure options outside of traditional GPUs.

item.title: Apple Intelligence registers with Chinese regulator for tablets and laptops
item.description: Apple's generative AI service, Apple Intelligence, has been registered for use on tablets and laptops with China's cyberspace regulator in Shanghai. China requires large language models and generative AI services to be registered with regulators before public release. This registration marks a step toward expanding Apple's AI features to tablets and laptops in China, following its previous iPhone approval.

item.title: Adobe integrates CX Enterprise Coworker into ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini
item.description: Adobe embedded its CX Enterprise Coworker agent into platforms including ChatGPT, Claude, Databricks Genie, Gemini for business, and Microsoft Copilot. The AI agent helps marketing teams orchestrate customer experiences using open standards like MCP and A2A. This integration allows enterprise marketing teams to access specialized customer experience workflows directly inside the third-party AI assistants they already use.

item.title: Sarvam AI appoints ex-Google Cloud India MD Sashikumar Sreedharan as President and CBO
item.description: Indian AI startup Sarvam AI appointed former Google Cloud India Managing Director Sashikumar Sreedharan as President and Chief Business Officer. Sreedharan brings over three decades of technology industry experience to his new roles on the executive team and board of directors. The executive appointment brings a seasoned tech industry leader to a prominent Indian AI startup as it expands its enterprise and government customer base.

item.title: AI replacement of human workers complicates manager pay and grading
item.description: As companies replace human workers with AI agents, determining managers' grade and pay is becoming harder. Both pay and grade often depend on how many people a manager supervises, according to Pilita Clark of the Financial Times. It highlights an overlooked operational challenge for organizations restructuring their workforces around AI tools.

item.title: Ada and Dialpad merge to combine AI customer service software
item.description: Toronto-based Ada and California-based Dialpad have agreed to merge their AI customer service and communications software businesses. The all-share transaction values Ada at approximately $600 million CAD. This merger combines two established players in the AI customer service and business communications market, reshaping the competitive landscape against other venture-backed startups.

item.title: Googlebook November update frees up 3GB-6GB of RAM via on-device AI optimizations
item.description: Google released its November update for Googlebook OS, which frees up 3GB to 6GB of system RAM through on-device AI memory optimizations. The update also improves browser memory management and patches approximately 60 Android flaws. The update addresses multitasking stability and memory consumption issues for Googlebook devices equipped with 16GB of RAM.

item.title: Trump says AI risks can be managed, signals openness to guardrails
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated that artificial intelligence risks can be managed and expressed openness to safeguards. He told CBS’s “60 Minutes” that he does not mind guardrails, provided they do not place the United States behind China. It signals a potential shift in US policy toward artificial intelligence safeguards while balancing international competition against China.

item.title: ByteDance considers data center expansion in Ceará, Brazil
item.description: ByteDance is considering expanding its data center project in Ceará, Brazil, with a second phase that would be larger than its ongoing 300-megawatt project. The TikTok owner is looking for developers to build the expansion. This expansion reflects the growing infrastructure investments by major technology companies in South America to support their operations.

item.title: Nvidia board investigates CEO Jensen Huang over affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who U.S. officials allege is a Chinese spy. The board stated it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. The investigation places the leadership of Nvidia at the center of a geopolitical and corporate governance crisis, raising questions about the stability of a central pillar of the global AI economy.

item.title: NVIDIA and South Korea expand sovereign AI and physical AI collaboration
item.description: NVIDIA and South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT are expanding their collaboration across sovereign AI infrastructure, data centers, models, and talent development. Major Korean industry leaders including Samsung, LG, SK Telecom, Kakao Mobility, and Hyundai Motor Group are integrating NVIDIA accelerated computing, simulation software, autonomous driving platforms, and security tools. The expanded partnership demonstrates how national governments and major technology firms are collaborating to build local AI ecosystems using accelerated computing and secure agentic workflows.

item.title: Cognition CISO Alex Stamos on how AI is upending cybersecurity
item.description: Nilay Patel interviewed Cognition CISO Alex Stamos on The Verge's Decoder podcast about how artificial intelligence is disrupting cybersecurity. Stamos discussed how AI-powered tools are being used by private and state actors to detect and exploit vulnerabilities simultaneously. It highlights how the widespread use of artificial intelligence in cyberattacks is forcing a major reevaluation of traditional security practices and defense strategies.

item.title: IT firms with lower capital requirements may gain as investors shift focus to AI monetisation: Report
item.description: According to an Anand Rathi report, IT companies capable of monetising enterprise AI without substantial capital investments may gain an advantage. Investors are increasingly differentiating between businesses funding AI infrastructure and those generating returns from its adoption. It shows that market focus is shifting from infrastructure spending to proven returns on investment in enterprise AI.

item.title: Tencent's chief AI scientist warns AI bio capabilities will soon risk harm
item.description: Tencent's chief AI scientist Yao Shunyu stated that artificial intelligence models will soon master biology and present safety risks. He spoke at a science event in Hong Kong following Tencent's launch of its new flagship model, Hy4. The warning highlights growing concern among major AI lab leaders regarding the dual-use biological risks of advanced models and the debate between open and closed development approaches.

item.title: India's GCCs and IT firms form enterprise AI partnerships
item.description: Global Capability Centres and Indian IT services firms are forming partnerships to deploy enterprise AI and integrate solutions across large organizations. A new study by ANSR and HFS Research scored India's GCC ecosystem at 61.9, noting that 83% of GCCs are mission-critical while only 17% have full budget authority. This trend highlights how multinational companies are combining in-house innovation hubs with traditional IT service providers to manage large-scale AI adoption and legacy system integration.

item.title: South Korea says Nvidia issues won't affect contracted GPU supplies
item.description: South Korea expects its contracted deliveries of Nvidia graphics processing units to proceed without disruption despite a controversy involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Vice Minister of Science and ICT Ryu Jemyung stated that 10,000 GPUs funded under a 2025 budget have already arrived and are in use. This reassures stakeholders that government-backed AI infrastructure procurement in South Korea remains stable amid corporate governance investigations at Nvidia.

item.title: US AI safety center officials asked to informally report to White House
item.description: Officials at the Commerce Department's AI safety center CAISSI were asked to informally report to a White House office, raising independence concerns. The division evaluates AI safety and standards with a $10 million annual budget. This development highlights concerns over the political independence of federal AI safety evaluations and oversight of commercial super-intelligence systems.
